title: Fixed rules headers sort on the first click and flip on every click after
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42 a-cat) exists.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42 b-cat) exists.
  • Category {Category-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42 c-cat) exists.
  • Fixed rule part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42-1) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-B} with fixed price (for example 30000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42-2) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-C} with fixed price (for example 10000.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC42-3) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 20000.00).
  • No other fixed rule at {Location-A} has a fixed price of 10,000 or more.
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Fixed rules tab.
  3. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  4. Click the Category column header.
  5. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  6. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  7. Click the Category column header again.
  8. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  9. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  10. Click the Category column header a third time.
  11. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  12. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  13. Click the Category column header a fourth time.
  14. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  15. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  16. Click the Fixed Price column header.
  17. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  18. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  19. Click the Fixed Price column header again.
  20. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  21. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  22. Click the Fixed Price column header a third time.
  23. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  24. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  25. Click the Part Number column header.
  26. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  27. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  28. Click the Part Number column header again.
  29. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  30. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
  31. Click the Part Number column header a third time.
  32. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  33. Read all three headers and the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: the first click on Category sorts A to Z. Only Category shows an arrow, pointing up. The rows read {Part-C} ({Category-A}), {Part-A} ({Category-B}), {Part-B} ({Category-C}).
  • Step 9: the second click flips it to Z to A. Only Category shows an arrow, pointing down. The rows read {Part-B}, {Part-A}, {Part-C}.
  • Step 12: the third click gives the same order as the first click (step 6). Only Category shows an arrow, pointing up, and the rows read {Part-C}, {Part-A}, {Part-B}. The list does not go back to its opening Part Number order.
  • Step 15: the fourth click flips it again. Only Category shows an arrow, pointing down, and the rows read {Part-B}, {Part-A}, {Part-C}.
  • Step 18: the first click on Fixed Price puts the highest price first. Only Fixed Price shows an arrow, pointing down (highest first is the descending direction). The first three rows of the list read {Part-A}, {Part-C}, {Part-B} (with the examples 30,000 > 20,000 > 10,000).
  • Step 21: the second click puts the lowest price first. Only Fixed Price shows an arrow, pointing up. {Part-B}, {Part-C}, {Part-A} are now the last three rows, in that order (10,000 < 20,000 < 30,000).
  • Step 24: the third click gives the same order as the first click (step 18). Only Fixed Price shows an arrow, pointing down, and the first three rows read {Part-A}, {Part-C}, {Part-B}.
  • Step 27: the first click on Part Number sorts A to Z. Only Part Number shows an arrow, pointing up. The rows read {Part-A}, {Part-B}, {Part-C}.
  • Step 30: the second click flips it to Z to A. Only Part Number shows an arrow, pointing down. The rows read {Part-C}, {Part-B}, {Part-A}.
  • Step 33: the third click gives the same order as the first click (step 27). Only Part Number shows an arrow, pointing up, and the rows read {Part-A}, {Part-B}, {Part-C}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10136 (Story 3, Fixed Rules, sortable columns; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S3-R1, S3-R2, S3-R3, S3-R4, S3-R5, S3-R5a, S3-R8, S3-R9, S3-R10, S3-R11, §2 Sort arrows, §4 Key Decisions ('A header toggles; there is no third state', 'Fixed price opens on the highest price'), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.4 (Fixed rules - before and after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Story SV-10136 acceptance criteria (re-synced 13 Oct 2026) agree: third click gives the first click's order, highest price first for Fixed price. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists). The technical plan of 13 Oct 2026 (FR-018, FR-020) says the first click on Fixed price sorts lowest first; PRD version 21 (14 Oct 2026, S3-R4, S3-R8) says highest first and is newer, so this case follows the PRD.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “The Part number column header is sortable.”
  • S3-R2: “The Category column header is sortable.”
  • S3-R3: “The Fixed price column header is sortable.”
  • S3-R4: “When the user clicks a sortable column header that is not currently sorted, the list sorts by that column: A to Z for Part number and Category, highest first for Fixed price (S3-R8).”
  • S3-R5: “When the user clicks that same header again, the list re-sorts in the opposite direction.”
  • S3-R5a: “A third click gives the same order as the first click. Every further click flips the direction again.”
  • S3-R8: “Fixed price sorts by value. Its first click puts the highest price first.”
  • S3-R9: “The second click on Fixed price puts the lowest price first.”
  • S3-R10: “Only one column is sorted at a time.”
  • S3-R11: “The column being sorted shows an arrow for the direction that is currently applied.”
  • PRD §2 Sort arrows: “A sortable column header shows an arrow when it is the column being sorted. The arrow points up for ascending and down for descending.”
  • PRD §2 Sort arrows: “Each click on the header being sorted flips its direction. A third click gives the same order as the first click. No click clears the sort or returns the list to its opening order.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “A header toggles; there is no third state. The first click sorts the column, the second reverses it, and the third gives the first click's order again.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “Fixed price opens on the highest price. Its first click puts the highest price first, like every money column in ShopView (Default Sorting, decided 2026-10-06).”
  • SV-10136 acceptance criteria: “Given the Category header is clicked, then the list sorts by category, its arrow is shown, and the Part number header shows no arrow.”
